whatItIs.text: Korea's fermented red-chili paste — sweet, savoury, and hot at once, built from chili powder, glutinous rice, fermented soybean powder, malt, and salt.

historyNote.text: A mid-9th-century Chinese document already records a Korean pepper paste, and a 1433 Korean medical text repeats it — though chillies only reached East Asia with Portuguese traders in the early 16th century, so the earliest pastes were a different kind of hot. Sunchang gochujang has been a palace-food legend since the founding of the Joseon dynasty.

howToChoose.text: Choose brands listing rice and meju (soybean) early — cheaper corn-syrup versions taste flatter; the paste should be brick-red and glossy, not neon.

storage.text: Refrigerate after opening and keep the rim clean; it keeps long but darkens.

useItUp.text: Whisk it with sesame oil, soy, and a little sugar for any marinade or stir-fry sauce; a spoonful turns mayo, butter, or broth into something worth dipping into.
